Your Excellencies, I'd like to thank Saudi Arabia, the European Union, and Norway for organizing this meeting. We are here today because we share the understanding that only collective and coordinated action in support of a political process can guarantee lasting peace for Israelis and Palestinians. The Gaza Peace Plan, UN Security Council Resolution 2803, the New York Declaration, and other relevant resolutions are the product of these efforts. And yet, one year after these commitments were made, we are at a point of serious escalation and regional confrontation. Only the first phase of the Gaza peace plan has been reached. We urge the parties to immediately and fully implement this plan and UN Security Council Resolution 2803, as well as to advance the commitments contained in the New York Declaration and in other relevant resolutions. Switzerland reiterates that all parties must respect international law. International humanitarian law must be respected in all circumstances, including the obligation to protect civilians and to facilitate rapid, safe, and unimpeded humanitarian access to and within the Gaza Strip. Last November, Switzerland decided on concrete measures to support the implementation of the Gaza peace plan and the New York Declaration. The government of Switzerland allocated an additional $28 million to three priority areas, humanitarian aid, strengthening Palestinian institutions, and promoting dialogue on regional stability. Switzerland also provides technical expertise through the deployment of experts to the International Gaza Support Centre and in support of local elections and related reforms in the occupied Palestinian territory. Switzerland continues to support a two-state solution based on international law. We contribute to discussions on disarmament and decommissioning, interfaith dialogue, and the inclusion of both Israeli and Palestinian civil society actors. Such inclusion is a key principle of Switzerland's peace promotion efforts worldwide. Only diplomacy grounded in international law and the implementation of agreements can build the trust necessary for lasting peace in the Middle East and beyond. Switzerland, true to its tradition of good offices, remains fully committed to supporting these efforts. Thank you very much.
Thank you, Excellency. I now give the floor to Her Excellency the Foreign Minister of Romania. You have the floor.

Your Excellency. A year has passed since we endorsed the New York Declaration on the Peaceful Settlement of the Question of Palestine and the Implementation of the Two-State Solution. Let me reaffirm from the beginning Romania's steadfast support and commitment for the two-state solutions. We are one of the countries in the world that has the longest standing uninterrupted diplomatic relationships with both Palestine and Israel, and we consider the two-state solution as the only viable framework for attaining a just, lasting, and comprehensive peace in the region. Until this shared vision is accomplished, the Global Alliance will continue to play a critical role. We see great value in adopting a holistic approach to the peace process, including through the coordination the Global Alliance initiatives with ongoing efforts by the Office of the High Representative for Gaza and the Board of Peace. While the current state of hostilities in the broader Middle East region remains a cause for continued concern for all of us. We shall avoid losing sight of the situation in Gaza as well as in the West Bank. And our citizens are also doing a great effort and campaign to remind politicians and keep us all committed on the fact that Gaza needs not just international attention, but also international solutions. We need to channel our efforts towards maintaining the current although fragile, ceasefire agreement and to move towards the implementation of the peace plan for Gaza and the UN CC resolution 2803. We hope to see substantial and steady progress in this regard, especially with the 15-point plan to disarm Hamas. We do hope that all actors will engage in credible negotiations to ensure the effective implementation of the coming period. The decommissioning of Hamas's weapons is a prerequisite for restoring long-term and security in Gaza. And the decommissioning of Hamas's weapons is also an instrument to attain support, trust, and involvement of the countries that are reluctant at this moment. The implementation of disarmament plan, as well as future arrangements, need to take into account also Israel's security concern and the legitimate right that the children, the families, the citizens need to feel safe today, need to feel safe. tomorrow. But that needs to happen within international law and progress towards peace and stability is the only way forward. We commend Palestinian Authority's constructive engagement in the implementation of the peace plan for Gaza. And we support enhanced coordination with and between the Palestinian Authority and the representatives of the National Committee for the Administration of Gaza. Our Romania's contribution to the stabilization and reconstruction efforts is on a couple of areas. We stand ready to support with the restoration of the emergency response infrastructure in Gaza. As we have started some time ago, the medical evacuation of children that need cancer treatment, we are going to continue to support in that respect as well. President Icahordan has mentioned Romania's commitment to the reconstruction of schools and our support for education, as well as supporting the Palestinian administration bodies in their capacity building efforts. We stand ready at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs as well to receive under scholarship diplomats from Palestine. Continue providing educational opportunities for the children and youth of Gaza by increasing the number of scholarships to Palestinian students as well. And as I have mentioned, we have organized more than 12 evacuation flights, and we will continue to do so in partnership with European countries and through the European Commission mechanism of civil intervention. At the same time, we call the Israeli government to adopt the necessary containment measures against the settlers' violence in the West Bank and refrain from further expanding the settlements, including in E1 area. As to the reform agenda of the Palestinian Authority, we welcome the progress and see effective and speedy implementation. We believe the reform program remains necessary for strengthening government's capacity and unimpeded access to the Palestinian tax revenue is a necessity and needs to be ensured. Let me conclude by underlining, once again, Romania's support to the two-state solution. And thank you for convening this very important conversation.
Thank you, Your Excellency. I now give the floor to His Excellency the Secretary General of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation. The floor is yours.

Thank you very much. Your Highness and Excellencies, I am pleased at the outset to express our sincere gratitude to the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, the European Union, and the Kingdom of Norway for convening this meeting. I would also like to thank all the participating states and organizations. This international momentum in support of the implementation of the New York Declaration on the two-state solution is highly appreciated. The Organization of Islamic Cooperation emphasized that the Israeli aggression, which continues to target the existence of the Palestinian people, their land, identity, and national rights, must stop. The implementation of the second phase of the peace plan and the Security Council Resolution 283 must begin in order to preserve the territorial contiguity of Palestine, ensure full withdrawal of the Israeli occupation forces, and commencement of reconstruction. This state must form part of a clear and integrated political track that is inseparable from the horizon of the final solution. The IEC also warns against the danger of the Israeli occupation policies in the occupied West Bank, which is aimed at undermining the two-state solution. The IEC welcomes the measure taken by several states toward illegal settlement and its products. It calls on other states of the world to activate all possible diplomatic legal and economic measures to prevent the consolidation of Israeli occupation and settlements. We also warn against the danger of Israeli violation against Islamic and Christian holy sites, particularly the blessed Al-Quds, Al-Aqsa Mosque. We reiterate that all Israeli schemes to Judaize Al-Quds is null and void under international law and must be stopped immediately. Your Excellencies, the OIC affirms its rejection of Israeli measures targeting the existence and legal mandate of UNRWA and its facilities. We call for political, legal, and financial support for UNRWA to enable it to continue its critical role in the service of the Palestinian refugees. We also warn against the danger, the continuous Israeli occupation measure to undermine the capability of the Palestinian government. We call for pressure to be applied for the full release of the illegally seized tax returns. We call for more support for the Palestinian government to enable it to exercise its responsibility and duties throughout the Palestinian territory. In conclusion, the IC renew its active and continuing engagement under this important international track. The IC appreciate the recognition of Palestine statehood by many states and calls on the remaining states of the world that are yet to take this step to do on the side of truth, justice. My last word will be to say that the Organization of Islamic Cooperation is also particularly pleased and proud of the leadership role taken by one of our founding members of OIC, the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, on this important and critical issue. We take this opportunity, Your Highness, Prince Faisal Al Saud, to congratulate you and the leadership of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia and the people of Saudi Arabia for the celebration of the National Day. Thank you very much.

Thank you, Excellency. I will now give the floor to His Excellency the Foreign Minister of Italy. After that, I will give the floor to His Excellency the High Commissioner for Human Rights, and that will end today's interventions. Thank you. Excellency, Italy, you have the floor.

Thank you very much. I want to thank you and Saudi Arabia for organizing another time this meeting with Norway. Thank you also for being in Rome during the last meeting for achieving this important goal to people, to states, as a priority for the Italian government. Today, we gather at a critical moment, only two months after our meeting. Italy thinks that it is crucial to keep the two-state perspective at the center of the international agenda, a solution that allows a Palestinian state and the state of Israel to live side by side in peace and security. We know that the road of dialogue and diplomacy is difficult. but this is the only way to reach peace, as I said yesterday during my speech in front of the plenary. In this context, Italy is also continuing to promote interreligious dialogue in the framework of the peace plan. Interreligious dialogue is a key tool to rebuild trust and promote reconciliation. First of all, we must consolidate the ceasefire in Gaza and address the humanitarian emergency. The roadmap for the disarmament of Hamas is a crucial step in the right direction. Now it is the time to advance on this. Hamas cannot have any role in the future of Gaza, and this disarmament is a chance also to strengthen humanitarian aid. Italy is in the first line in Gaza. Our Carabinieri are in the Rafah crossing in the European mission that we will lead from November the 1st. We must ensure the flow of humanitarian aid into the Strip and the start of the recovery and the reconstruction. Italy continues to provide humanitarian medical assistance and keep open our university corridors. A few days ago, we delivered 35 tons of emergency aid of food for Gaza to the Strip. Last week, a new group of 25 students arrived from Gaza to Italy to study in our best university. This is a concrete investment in the future Palestinian state. But we strongly condemn the violence of the settlers and the expansion of the settlements in the West Bank, first of all in E1. They put in danger the prospect of the two states. We are in first line in Brussels for a new sanctions against the settlers. We contributed with 10 million to the United Nations Trust Fund and we are ready to help on reforms. We will support the next legislative elections in Palestine, with a financial contribution of 1 million euro to UNDP. A future Palestinian state must also be economically sustainable. For this reason, it is key that Israel releases Palestinian tax revenues and ensures stable banking relations. dear colleagues, Italy is ready to work together with Israelis and the Palestinians and with all international partners for a future of peaceful coexistence, stability and prosperity. This is the vision that inspired our commitment to peace in the Middle East. This is the message we want to send today. Italy is ready to do its part. Count on us. Thank you very much, my friends.
Thank you, Excellency. And I now give the floor to His Excellency, Mr. Volker Turk. The floor is yours.

Shukran, Jazila, and Your Royal Highness, Excellencies, distinguished delegates. My office has been monitoring, documenting, and reporting on the human rights situation in the occupied Palestinian territory for the last 30 years. This is also fundamentally a question about international law and respect for international law. Israel's relentless violations of international law in the occupied Palestinian territory pose an existential threat to the two-state solution. If one looks, and we have just heard it, Israeli forces that are deployed in 70% of Gaza have killed some 1,400 Palestinians since the announcement of the ceasefire almost a year ago, according to figures from the Palestinian Ministry of Health. Much of the territory is a dystopian wasteland that can barely support human life. In the West Bank, settlers and Israeli forces regularly attack Palestinian communities, assault families, demolish property and expand settlements in breach of international law. And in case there was no doubt, some senior Israeli officials have repeatedly called for the forced displacement of all Palestinians from Gaza, Israeli sovereignty over the West Bank and an end to any possibility of a Palestinian state. We are close to a point of no return. So the two-state solution cannot wait any longer, and the international community has taken some steps towards its fulfillment, but they are clearly not enough. The New York Declaration offers a blueprint for implementing a two-state solution, and human rights offer the means to make that blueprint succeed. Human rights provide a shared legal framework and the foundations for legitimate governance, accountable institutions, participation, protection, and trust. Human rights safeguards need to include support for grassroots Palestinian and Israeli civil society groups that are focused on accountability, on justice and reconciliation. And I have met with organizations from each community and groups that represent both. And all told me there will never be sustainable peace without strong principled action by the international community. I heard this from both sides. States, therefore, need to apply real political pressure to prevent the entrenchment of Israel's unlawful presence in the occupied Palestinian territory. They need to do everything in their power to secure a future in which Palestinians and Israelis live side by side in equal dignity and rights, in line with UN resolutions and international law. Shukran Jazilan.

Thank you, Your Excellency. We have listened to a clear message today. There is a wide consensus on the two-state solution, but what is required now is to transform this to tangible measures on the ground, not to manage the conflict indefinitely, but to work to end the conflict through a just and lasting and comprehensive peace that guarantees peace for both Israelis and Palestinians. We are pleased to announce the adoption of the joint statement, which includes the salient messages from this meeting, and we thank you for your participation. The session is adjourned.
